body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students know that sh, ch, th, wh and ck each spell one sound (RF.1.3).
- Students read and write one-syllable words with consonant digraphs (RF.1.3).
- Students hear a digraph sound at the beginning or end of a spoken word (RF.1.2).

MATERIALS
- Letter buddy cards: sh, ch, th, wh, ck
- Picture cards: ship, shell, chin, chick, thumb, three, whale, wheel, duck, sock
- A pocket chart with two columns for sorting
- Tablets with the class activities open

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Letter Buddies together. Introduce sh and ch with a gesture for each (finger to lips for sh, a train arm for ch).
Day 2: Lesson activity: Meet the Letter Buddies. Add th and wh. Students say each word and name the buddy.
Day 3: Digraph Picture Sort: students draw a sh word and a ch word and tell about them.
Day 4: Introduce ck at the end of words (duck, sock). Students complete Fix the Word.
Day 5: Assessment: Letter Buddy Check. Read each word aloud twice. Reteach in a small group anyone who mixes up sh and ch.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: keep the gesture for each buddy on a card on the student's desk. Start with sh and ch only.
- Support: students can build the words in Fix the Word with letter cards before writing them.
- Stretch: find letter buddies at the end of words (wish, bench, bath) and write a silly sentence using three of them.
- Multilingual learners: th has no match in many languages. Show the tongue between the teeth with a mirror and keep practice playful.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week we are learning letter buddies: two letters that make one sound, like sh in ship, ch in chip, th in thumb, wh in whale and ck in duck. Go on a letter buddy hunt at home: can your child find sh or ch on a cereal box, a sign or a book?
title: Teacher guide: Two Letters, One Sound
